meta.temperature_K_convention: Pair is [min_K, max_K]. Use null for max to mean no upper bound. A number always means that number — there is no magic threshold. (999 is still read as no-bound for older files, but is deprecated: write null.)

general.description: Clusters of crystalline shards on cold, airless worlds far from the system's main star, in systems holding a life-bearing or water world.

species.description: Single-species genus, logged with the composition scanner. Cold (20-273 K), at least 12,000 Ls from the arrival star, in a system with an Earth-like, ammonia or water giant, or a gas giant with life.

conditions.parent_star: A, F, G, K, M, S or a brown dwarf (hostStarGates.ts)
matchContextNotes: Measured 2026-09-28 on the Spansh dump's 5,932 Shards bodies (DSS genus $Codex_Ent_Ground_Struct_Ice_Name;): every one is ≥ 12,004 Ls from the arrival star (the owner's 12,000 Ls rule, measured from the arrival star, not the body's own), 20-267 K, Icy 61 % / Rocky 23 % / HMC 14 % / Rocky Ice 2 %, never Metal-rich.
81 % airless; the rest thin Carbon dioxide, Neon, Neon-rich, Helium, Methane or Argon — listed, so those are not demoted.
Companion body: 245 of 259 systems the dump holds whole (94.6 %) have one of the listed classes; 4 of the 14 without have a Water World, which is added.

Every condition must be known and met (owner, 2026-10-04: no guesswork): until a body of a listed class has been scanned in the system, the host star is known and the distance from arrival is ≥ 12,000 Ls, Shards are not listed at all — not even as unlikely. A DSS naming the genus lists them regardless.
Host star: K, M, G, F, brown dwarfs and A — never O, B, white dwarf, neutron or black hole (hostStarGates.ts).

sources: Spansh galaxy dump, every body whose DSS genus list carries $Codex_Ent_Ground_Struct_Ice_Name;
